note: Built on two voices: Ruben Tagalog, the crooner of the radio show Harana ni Ruben Tagalog, from a Villar Records collection whose original recording dates are not on any page read (years left null), and the Harana Kings, three old provincial haranistas recorded with guitarist Florante Aguilar in 2012, singing Tagalog and Ilocano serenades (Dardarepdep, No Duaduaem Pay). Florante Aguilar's three tracks are solo-guitar versions of serenade songs, including the Cebuano Usahay and Matud Nila; Charmaine Clamor's Harana sa Dilim is a jazz singer's modern take.

size.basis: A judgement, not a count; no source counts recordings. Harana was sung live under windows, not made for records, and the practice has declined since the 1980s. What is on record: the 78s, radio and LP output of crooners such as Ruben Tagalog (a 12-track Villar Records 'Harana' collection) and Villar's Ilocano harana records by Felipe Alonzo; a handful of dedicated modern albums (Introducing the Harana Kings, 14 tracks, 2012; Florante Aguilar's The Art of Harana, 14 guitar serenades, 2003; Charmaine Clamor's My Harana, 12 jazz-leaning tracks, 2008); and a guitar series that mixes harana and kundiman (Raffy Lata, seven volumes, 2022-2026). Regional repertoires (Cebuano, Ilocano, Bicolano) add uncatalogued cassette and local releases. The many recent pop singles titled 'Harana' mostly are not the genre. An insider's essential list is about 30 recordings, most of them Ruben Tagalog and the Harana Kings.
